source.original_question:
In remote locations, photographers must keep track of their position from their base. One morning a photographer sets out from base, represented by point B, to the edge of an ice shelf at point S. She then walked to point P.

If the photographer were to walk back to her base from point P, what is the total distance she would have travelled? Round your answer to one decimal place.

adaptations.reason: Decorative scenery/icons removed; native mathematical lines, angle arcs, measurements and point relationships retained.

Source has an unlabeled bearing arc at B and is underdetermined. Added bearing55°to that arc, a consistent explicit completion that reproduces the source perimeter while retaining the navigation target.

independent_solution.method: Bearings55°and145°differ90°, giving right angleBSP. WithBP916, BS=916cos35° andSP=916sin35°. Total=916(1+cos35°+sin35°)=2191.699..., rounds2191.7m.
